title: Strengthening defence and security ties with Vietnam
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Strengthening defence and security ties with Vietnam Joint media release with: The Hon Anthony Albanese MP, Prime Minister of Australia The Hon Richard Marles MP, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister for Defence The Hon Tony Burke MP, Minister for Home Affairs, Minister for Cyber Security, Minister for Immigration and Citizenship, Minister for the Arts 11 August 2026 Australia and Vietnam have agreed to bolster defence and security cooperation to support our shared commitment to a peaceful, stable and prosperous region. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and General Secretary of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Vietnam and President of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, His Excellency Mr To Lam issued the Joint Statement on Deepening the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between Australia and Vietnam, reinforcing cooperation on shared priorities including defence and security. As part of the visit, the two countries announced new practical measures to strengthen defence and security cooperation. Australia and Vietnam's Ministers for Defence agreed to an updated Joint Vision Statement on Defence Cooperation to support closer exchanges, including across maritime security and disaster relief. Australian and Vietnamese defence forces will work more closely together, including by sharing expertise on search and rescue operations and participating in joint training. Respective border agencies signed memoranda of understanding for further work together to combat transnational crime, strengthen border protection and enhance maritime cooperation. Quotes attributable to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese: "Australia and Vietnam are close partners and we are both committed to a peaceful, stable and prosperous region. "These new agreements deliver practical cooperation between our countries and help ensure we can meet the challenges of an increasingly complex strategic environment." Quotes attributable to Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles: "Vietnam is an important defence partner for Australia, and we are committed to deepening cooperation in ways that directly contribute to the stability and security of our region. "By expanding practical cooperation across areas such as maritime security, search and rescue, disaster relief and training, we are building stronger capabilities and closer ties between our two defence forces." Quotes attributable to Minister for Foreign Affairs Penny Wong: "Australia and Vietnam are strengthening our defence and security ties as result of the growing strategic trust under our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. "We both share a commitment to a region where countries can make their own decisions, sovereignty is respected, and disputes can be managed peacefully." Quotes attributable to Minister for Home Affairs Tony Burke: "The threats we're facing today do not stop at national borders. If cyber criminals and organised crime gangs are going to function on a transnational basis, then our response needs to be transnational as well. "One country alone can't deal with these growing threats. Strong cooperation with trusted partners is essential to keep our communities safe." title: Funding doubled for Logan Medicare Mental Health Centre
text: Funding doubled for Logan Medicare Mental Health Centre 30 July 2026 Funding doubled for Logan Medicare Mental Health Centre Note Joint media release with The Hon Emma McBride MP Assistant Minister for Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Assistant Minister for Rural and Regional Health The Albanese Government is more than doubling funding for the Logan Medicare Mental Health Centre to provide expanded access to mental health care in the local community. This is about making sure locals get access to dedicated mental health services where they need it and when they need it. It means much more funding that will deliver more affordable healthcare for more people in our local community at no cost to patients. The $10.9 million upgrade will double the service capability for the Logan Medicare Mental Health Centre, including 16 additional clinical and non‑clinical staff. Since opening in late 2024, the Logan Medicare Mental Health Centre has provided 3000 free, walk in appointments. Once the upgrade is complete in mid‑2027, the centre will have capacity for 6000 appointments per year. More patients will be able to access coordinated, tailored support from psychologists, GPs, social workers and counsellors in one place. This investment is part of the Government’s $267.3 million commitment to deliver 32 new or upgraded Medicare Mental Health Centres in the heart of local communities across Australia by 2029–30. By mid‑2030, 92 Medicare Mental Health Centres will be operating across Australia. In Queensland, the Albanese Government is establishing 24 centres, with 17 already open, including in Ipswich, Redlands, Strathpine, Inner North Brisbane, Redcliffe and Caboolture. Medicare Mental Health Centres provide free mental health care and support to anyone, without the need for an appointment or referral. The Logan Medicare Mental Health Centre is fully funded by the Australian Government and services are provided by Footprints Community. More funding for more Medicare mental health services is just one of many ways we’re delivering for our local community in the Budget. We’re delivering for the people of Logan and the southern suburbs of Brisbane with more tax cuts for local workers, more cost‑of‑living relief and more help for first homebuyers to get into the housing market. We’ll continue to deliver for our community and deliver real change for the country, with more tax cuts, more cost‑of‑living relief and more investment to strengthen Medicare like the big boost for mental health services we’re announcing today. The Hon Dr Jim Chalmers MP Treasurer

title: 49 young people appointed to 2026 Youth Advisory Groups
text: Release type: Media Release Date: 23 March 2026 49 young people appointed to 2026 Youth Advisory Groups Ministers: Senator the Hon Dr Jess Walsh Minister for Early Childhood Education Minister for Youth Forty-nine young Australians will come together in Canberra this week to begin working with and advising the Albanese Labor Government on key policy issues as part of the 2026 Youth Advisory Groups. The Advisory Group members, together with the Youth Steering Committee, will meet with Ministers, their respective departments and Members of Parliament as part of Youth Meets Parliament Week. Aged 16 to 24, the 2026 cohort was selected from more than 500 applicants nationwide and brings diverse lived experience to the policy issues that matter most to young Australians. Youth Meets Parliament Week and the 2026 Youth Advisory Groups provide an important opportunity for the young representatives to engage with the Government and key decision‑makers directly and to work together to drive better policy outcomes. The 2026 Youth Advisory Groups members represent the breadth of diversity among Australia’s young people and their experiences. This includes First Nations young people, members from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, members with experience of mental ill-health, young people living in regional, rural and remote Australia, young migrants, gender diverse members, young parents, members with experience of being a carer, members from LGBTIQA+ communities, and members with disabilities. For more information visit youth.gov.au . Quotes attributable to the Minister for Youth, Jess Walsh: “Congratulations to all the new members of the Youth Advisory Groups and I look forward to working with them this year. “Being selected to be part of these committees is no easy feat. “This is a wonderful opportunity for young people to have a say on the policies and programs that affect them. “These young people have a lot to offer, and we can deliver better outcomes by listening to their valuable insights and lived experience. “That’s what Youth Meets Parliament Week is all about – bringing together youth representatives and Ministers and Members of Parliament in Canberra so we can listen to what they have to say.” For more information on the 2026 Youth Advisory Group members visit youth.gov.au/youth-advisory-groups Youth Advisory title: Humanitarian assistance in response to earthquakes in Venezuela
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Humanitarian assistance in response to earthquakes in Venezuela Joint media release with: The Hon Dr Anne Aly MP, Minister For Small Business, International Development And Multicultural Affairs 02 July 2026 The Australian Government will provide $2 million in humanitarian assistance to support communities affected by the earthquakes that struck Venezuela on 24 June 2026. While the full scale of this tragedy is still emerging, the devastation is widespread. The confirmed fatalities are in the thousands, and tens of thousands more remain missing. The death toll is expected to increase in the coming days as rescue teams continue their work. With the destruction of homes and critical infrastructure, nearly two million people are estimated to be in need of humanitarian assistance. These earthquakes also exacerbate an already serious humanitarian situation resulting from Venezuela’s economic situation. Australia’s funding will contribute, alongside international partners including the United States, United Kingdom and the European Union, to emergency food, shelter, water, sanitation, hygiene, and psychosocial support. The funding will also assist first responders, local authorities and humanitarian partners with transport, storage, coordination and logistics. Our assistance will be delivered through trusted partners, including the International Federation of the Red Cross and the United Nations World Food Programme. This latest funding is additional to Australia’s contributions to the UN Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) and the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement’s Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF), which have already released funding to support the emergency response. Quotes attributable to the Minister for Foreign Affairs Penny Wong: "Our thoughts are with the people of Venezuela, the Australian-Venezuelan community, and all those affected by the devastating earthquakes in Venezuela. "Australia’s humanitarian assistance will support access to food, shelter, medical care and other essential services." Quotes attributable to the Minister for International Development Dr Anne Aly: "Australia is working with our humanitarian partners to provide life-saving assistance for civilians affected by the recent earthquakes in Venezuela. "My thoughts are with the people of Venezuela, and the diaspora community in Australia, and around the world who have been affected by this devastating disaster." title: Business investment booming under Labor
text: Business investment booming under Labor 28 May 2026 Business investment booming under Labor New figures released by the ABS today show private sector investment is soaring under the Albanese Labor Government. Capital expenditure has far exceeded market expectations, with billions more being poured into productive investments. This is good news for Australian businesses and good news for our economy. New private capital expenditure (capex) grew very strongly at 6.5 per cent in the March quarter – more than six times the median market expectation. It means capex is up 14.6 per cent through the year. Data centres, renewable energy and battery storage drove non‑mining capex, which grew 8.8 per cent through the quarter and is up 20.9 per cent through the year. These kinds of infrastructure projects are a priority for our government, and clearly, they’re a priority for the private sector as well. We know capex can be lumpy, but these very welcome figures come despite the economic uncertainty caused by the war in the Middle East. Even before these numbers, business investment was growing by an average of 3.9 per cent under this Labor Government after going backwards 1.3 per cent under the Coalition. These figures once again show we’re well placed and well prepared to confront this global uncertainty and volatility, with faster growth than any major advanced economy at the end of last year, low unemployment, solid wages growth and stronger public finances. This is another important reminder that some people should stop talking our economy down. In our most recent Budget, the Albanese Government announced $3.5 billion in business tax relief measures to encourage more private investment. This includes making the small business instant asset write‑off permanent, introducing two‑year loss carry back for companies with turnover of up to $1 billion, introducing loss refundability and expanding incentives for venture capital. These measures are all about giving businesses the confidence to invest and will support a more productive and resilient economy. The Hon Dr Jim Chalmers MP Treasurer

title: Joint media release: Building Australia's fuel security with strategic fuel reserves and low carbon liquid fuels
text: Joint media release: Building Australia's fuel security with strategic fuel reserves and low carbon liquid fuels Joint media release: Building Australia's fuel security with strategic fuel reserves and low carbon liquid fuels 18 August 2026 The Hon Chris Bowen MP, Minister for Climate Change and Energy The Hon Catherine King MP, Minister for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government The Hon Julie Collins MP, Minister for Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry The Albanese Government's $14.8 billion Fuel Security and Resilience Package will protect Australians from global fuel shocks, put downward pressure on costs and accelerate the transition to our own home-grown, sovereign fuels. Today, the Government is releasing two consultation papers that will help shape the next phase of Australia's fuel security agenda, ensuring the nation has the supplies it needs when they matter most while building a stronger domestic fuel industry for the future. Announced in the 2026-27 Budget, the Fuel Security and Resilience Package is Australia's most significant investment in fuel security, strengthening the nation's resilience against international disruptions while creating new economic opportunities for Australian industry and regional communities. The Strengthening Australia's Fuel Security and Resilience Consultation Paper seeks feedback on key design features of three major measures that underpin the Government's approach to fuel security: establishing the Australian Fuel Security Reserve increasing the Minimum Stockholding Obligation backed by co-investment in fuel storage supporting the continued operation of Australia's two remaining domestic refineries beyond 2030. The Government is investing $3.2 billion to establish the Australian Fuel Security Reserve, creating a government-owned strategic reserve of one billion litres of diesel and jet fuel. The reserve will provide an additional safeguard against international supply disruptions and fuel market volatility, helping ensure Australians have access to the fuel they need when global markets come under pressure. The Government has also committed to increasing mandatory industry fuel stockholding requirements by an additional 10 days for diesel, petrol and jet fuel by 2030. By requiring higher fuel stockholdings, we will be better positioned to withstand supply disruptions and maintain reliable access to fuel for households, businesses and critical industries. The consultation also seeks views on options to support Australia's two remaining domestic refineries to continue operating beyond 2030, recognising the important role domestic refining plays in strengthening fuel security and sovereign capability. The Securing Australia's Cleaner Fuels Industry Consultation Paper seeks feedback on options to grow Australia's domestic Low Carbon Liquid Fuels (LCLF) industry and reduce reliance on imported fuels. The consultation is seeking views on a potential demand mechanism, including the level of ambition and how it could be implemented, impacts for businesses and consumers and the evidence required to inform key policy decisions. A stronger domestic low carbon liquid fuels industry represents a significant opportunity for Australia to diversify supply and produce more of the fuels we need here at home, creating jobs, attracting investment and strengthening regional economies. It will also play an important role in reducing emissions in sectors where electrification is difficult, including aviation, heavy transport, mining and agriculture, supporting Australia's transition to net zero while maintaining economic competitiveness. Together, these measures will help secure Australia's fuel future by ensuring reliable supplies, supporting domestic industry and building the cleaner fuels needed to drive future growth. The consultation papers are available on the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water's Have Your Say platform. The Securing Australia's Cleaner Fuels Industry Consultation Paper can be found here: https://consult.dcceew.gov.au/securing-australias-cleaner-fuels-industry-consultation The Strengthening Australia's Fuel Security and Resilience Consultation Paper can be found here: https://consult.dcceew.gov.au/australias-fuel-security-and-resilience-package Quotes attributable to Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen : “Australia cannot afford to be vulnerable to fuel supply disruptions beyond our shores. That's why we’re making a historic investment to strengthen fuel security, support domestic refining and build the cleaner fuels industries of the future. “We're strengthening Australia's resilience by building larger fuel reserves, increasing stockholdings and backing domestic industry to produce more of the fuels we need here at home. “By strengthening fuel security today and building cleaner fuel industries for tomorrow, we're delivering practical economic and environmental benefits for Australian households, businesses and communities.” Quotes attributable to Minister for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government Catherine King: “We are investing in the fuels our aviation, maritime and freight industries need. “Currently, we export up to $6 billion of feedstocks each year, including canola and tallow, for global markets. “By building a low carbon liquid fuels industry right here, we will create more jobs, build regional economies, strengthen our fuel security and future-proof our transport industries.” Quotes attributable to Minister for Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry, Julie Collins: “Fuel security is about making sure Australian communities, families, businesses and industries can rely on the supplies they need – including our farmers and producers. “This investment will help strengthen our resilience to global disruptions and provide Australia with critical and reliable fuel to keep our food production strong “Building more domestic fuel production creates an exciting opportunity to add value to Australian feedstocks bringing more opportunities for our farmers and foresters.”

title: More than 50,000 families supported to give their babies the best start in life
text: Media event date: 7 August 2026 Date published: 7 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Australian Government is helping Australian families access trusted breastfeeding advice and support, with more than 50,000 families turning to the National Breastfeeding Helpline last year. As Australia marks World Breastfeeding Week, the National Breastfeeding Helpline and LiveChat Service continue to provide free, professional and non-judgemental support to parents and carers with feeding questions and breastfeeding challenges from pregnancy through to early childhood. Breastfeeding can give babies a strong start in life, supporting healthy growth and development and helping protect against a range of illnesses. It also has important health benefits for mothers, including reducing the risk of breast and ovarian cancers and supporting recovery after childbirth. While breastfeeding can be a rewarding experience, it is not always easy. Whether it is a late-night feeding concern, questions about milk supply or simply a need for reassurance, the National Breastfeeding Helpline connects families with trained counsellors who have breastfed themselves and understand the questions and pressures that can come with it. Operated by the Australian Breastfeeding Association, the National Breastfeeding Helpline and LiveChat Service are available 24 hours a day, helping parents and carers access evidence-based information, practical advice and support whenever they need it. Since 2008, the National Breastfeeding Helpline has received more than 1.2 million calls, making it one of Australia's most accessible sources of breastfeeding information and support. The service is delivered by 465 trained volunteer counsellors with personal breastfeeding experience. In the past 12 months, 43 per cent of callers reported the service helped them avoid a visit to a GP or other health service, showing how timely advice and reassurance can support families early. The Australian Government has funded the National Breastfeeding Helpline since 2008 and LiveChat since 2018 and is investing a further $8.9 million to ensure these services remain available to families across Australia. Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister White “Breastfeeding has lifelong benefits for both mothers and babies, but many parents need support along the way. Many parents have questions, especially in those early days and weeks, and it’s important they know support is available. “The National Breastfeeding Helpline gives families trusted, practical advice from trained counsellors who understand the challenges parents can face. “Whether you live in a major city, a regional town or a remote community, support is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week.” Attributable to Australia Breastfeeding Association, Executive Officer, Victoria Marshall-Cerins “Every call and chat matters, our volunteers are available around the clock every day of the year. We provide a service that thousands of families rely on. “Calls are generally answered within 3 minutes by our incredible volunteers, many even sooner. It is a free service, families can call for reassurance, support, and care without having to leave the home.” Minister: The Hon Rebecca White MP Tags: Pregnancy, birth and baby

title: Student visa integrity reforms take effect today
text: Release type: Media Release Date: 2 October 2026 Student visa integrity reforms take effect today Ministers: The Hon Julian Hill MP Assistant Minister for International Education Assistant Minister for Citizenship, Customs and Multicultural Affairs The Albanese Labor Government is strengthening the student visa program to curtail visa hopping, protect Australia’s premium international education sector, and ensure the migration system operates in the national interest. International education is a national asset, supporting jobs and the education of domestic students, funding research, growing the economy, enriching communities and building lifelong human connections between Australia and the world. Ensuring the quality and integrity of Australia’s international education sector is essential to maintain the nation’s reputation as a global leader in international education. New measures will target misuse while reinforcing the Student visa’s core purpose: temporary stay for study. The reforms will: limit onshore Student visa applications remove the ability of most students to bring family members, with only limited exceptions in the national interest extend transfer restrictions between education providers, remove the ability of students to come to Australia for Higher Education and transfer onshore to VET, and introduce a new Student visa transfer stream in 2027. Stopping visa hopping Onshore Student visa applications will be limited to genuine cases: Most temporary visa holders, including Working Holiday Maker and Skills in Demand visa holders, will no longer be able to apply for a Student visa in Australia. Student visa holders seeking another onshore Student visa must demonstrate genuine course progression. Limited exemptions will apply, including for school and PhD students, and students affected by provider default or course deferral. Keeping family settings focused Student visa applicants will face tighter rules on including partners and children, helping ensure student visas are mainly granted to people who are coming to Australia to study. Limited exemptions will apply to: PhD students; nationals of Pacific and ASEAN member countries; and students sponsored by Australian or foreign governments. Families already together in Australia will not be separated so eligible Student visa holders applying for a new onshore visa may include only family members already here. In these limited circumstances where family members are able to accompany a student, applicants will need to apply at the time the primary student applies, as the ability of any students to add ‘subsequent entrants’ has now been removed for all students. Similar restrictions will apply to Temporary Graduate visas. The changes will not separate families already in Australia where family members hold Student or Temporary Graduate visas as secondary applicants. Closing transfer loopholes From mid-2027, international students seeking to change providers after arriving in Australia will need to apply through a new Student visa transfer stream. The new stream will prevent transfers to lower-level courses that bypass evidence requirements and disrupt the business models of providers targeting students with low-cost or lower-quality courses after they arrive in Australia. From today, as a transition measure until 30 June 2027 when the new transfer visa takes effect, the Government has amended the rules restricting overseas student transfers between providers, so that non-school students must remain in their principal course for 12 months before seeking a transfer, up from six months. School students will remain subject to the existing six-month restriction for their first registered school course. Transfers will still be allowed in exceptional circumstances or where a provider or course ceases to be registered. From 1 July 2027, students applying for a new Student visa in the transfer stream will have to have received their new visa before they can commence study at a new provider, the end date of their new visa will remain the same. The reforms only allow transfers at level or up the Australian Qualification Framework and Students will no longer be able to come to Australia to study Higher Education and transfer onshore to VET. A firm, balanced approach These reforms protect a strong, sustainable international education sector while ensuring visa programs are used as intended. Australia continues to welcome genuine students, support quality education, and maintain a migration system that is fair, trusted and in the national interest. Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister for International Education, Citizenship, Customs and Multicultural affairs, Hon. Julian Hill MP: “Australia’s international education sector is a national asset, and continued success depends on a ruthless focus on quality, integrity and a great student experience for those who seek value in a premium Australian education. “This is a sweeping package of reforms that gets the balance right to tighten integrity, manage numbers in a sensible way without trashing one of our nation’s largest and proudest export sectors as some loud, ill-informed voices seek to do. “Having inherited a mess from the Liberals in 2022, the Albanese Government won’t take a backwards step in managing the size and the shape of the onshore student market in the national interest. “Extending the transfer restriction to 12 months as an interim measure until the new student transfer visa comes in on 1 July 2027 delivers immediate action on unacceptably high onshore transfer activity, while preserving transfers for legitimate reasons.” Share on: facebook twitter email print

title: Next Tranche of Tax Reforms Pass the Parliament
text: Next Tranche of Tax Reforms Pass the Parliament 19 August 2026 Next Tranche of Tax Reforms Pass the Parliament The Albanese government has delivered more of our ambitious tax reform agenda with the second tranche of legislation passing the Senate today. These reforms deliver billions of dollars in support for business to encourage productive investment and sensible risk taking. This is great news for small businesses across the country and will help drive investment, innovation and resilience across the economy. This legislation delivers on two more of the government’s $3.8 billion in new measures that lower taxes for businesses and start‑ups. The legislation also includes the further implementation details we flagged at the outset of the tax reform process, providing certainty for people who acquire an interest in property as a result of inheritance or relationship breakdown. We said we’d address these issues and we’ve delivered on that today. The Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 2) Bill 2026 reintroduces loss carry‑back for companies for tax years starting on or after 1 July 2026. Loss carry‑back enables eligible companies to offset a loss against tax paid up to two years earlier, generating a refundable tax offset. This will deliver more help to 85,000 mostly small businesses, supporting productive investment and sensible risk‑taking and providing timely cash flow support to bolster resilience as well. The Bill also makes the $20,000 small business instant asset write‑off permanent from 1 July 2026. The Albanese government has now delivered certainty to small businesses who have for too long had to wait to see if the Parliament would extend the instant asset write off each year. All 2.7 million active small businesses with turnover of less than $10 million stand to benefit. This will reduce compliance costs for small business by around $32 million per year and provide the certainty small businesses need to invest with confidence. The Bill builds on the legislation to reform negative gearing and capital gains tax passed in June. It ensures a property owned on Budget night will retain access to negative gearing in certain circumstances. The provisions in the Bill ensure an individual can retain this treatment for an ownership interest in a property where: the property was acquired from a spouse through an inheritance or relationship breakdown; or someone inherits part or all of a property in which they already had an ownership share. They also ensure new builds will retain access to negative gearing and concessional capital gains tax treatment in the same circumstances. The Government released drafts of these amendments on 4 August for consultation, reflecting our intention to consult on the more complex aspects of these reforms. Legislating significant reforms in tranches is a standard approach, and we’ll continue to deliver more tranches of reform in the coming months, consistent with past reforms such as the GST and other major changes. Our reforms are all about making our economy work in the interests of more Australians, businesses and future generations, delivering more support for small business, more tax cuts for workers, and making it easier for Australians to buy their first home. The Hon Dr Jim Chalmers MP Treasurer

title: Exposure draft legislation – Minimum tax on discretionary trusts
text: Exposure draft legislation – Minimum tax on discretionary trusts 3 September 2026 Exposure draft legislation – Minimum tax on discretionary trusts The Albanese Government is today releasing draft legislation to implement the core components of the minimum tax on discretionary trusts announced in the 2026–27 Budget. We’re delivering a fairer tax system and helping fund tax cuts for workers by better aligning the tax rate on trust income with tax rates paid by workers. The draft legislation builds on the consultation paper released in July and includes expanded options to limit or eliminate restructuring costs for small businesses and others using discretionary trusts. This includes a new option for discretionary trusts to be exempt from the minimum tax if they elect to make fixed distributions to pre‑nominated beneficiaries, as an alternative to roll‑over relief. The election would not require a restructure and is not expected to result in state and territory stamp duties. The Government has been clear that a range of trust types will be excluded including charitable trusts, special disability trusts and superannuation funds, as well as primary production income and certain income relating to vulnerable minors. Deceased estates and all discretionary testamentary trusts established for genuine testamentary purposes will also be excluded. The draft legislation also ensures that all distributions from trusts to registered charities and deductible gift recipients (DGRs) are also exempt. Distributions to other income tax‑exempt entities like sporting clubs will also be exempt, up to a reasonable cap to be finalised following consultation. The draft legislation also sets out other implementation details including: A new definition of fixed trusts to help ensure a range of commercial trust types that do not have material discretionary elements are not captured by the minimum tax. This includes widely held trusts, managed investment trusts, bare trusts and employee share trusts. Details of the expanded roll‑over relief that will be available for three years from 1 July 2027 to assist taxpayers that wish to restructure out of a discretionary trust into other arrangements. Refunds for franking credits that relate to income subject to the minimum tax, which remain after the trustee has offset its income tax liabilities. Less than 10 per cent of Australia’s 2.7 million active small businesses will be affected by these reforms in any given year. Consistent with other significant tax reforms, the Government will continue to finalise implementation of these changes in further tranches of legislation, including administrative and integrity arrangements as necessary. Legislation to address implementation of the 2018 Budget measure on unpaid present entitlements that was announced but not enacted by the previous Government will be progressed separately. The Government thanks the many stakeholders and community members who have already contributed to the consultation process and invites further feedback on this reform. The exposure draft materials are available on the Treasury consultation hub , along with contact details for stakeholders who have questions or wish to discuss the materials with Treasury before lodging a submission. Consultation is open until 18 September 2026 with interested stakeholders encouraged to reach out to Treasury early in the consultation period. We’re big supporters of small business and the Government’s tax reform package includes over $3.8 billion in new measures that lower taxes on business to support investment and growth. This includes legislation making the $20,000 instant asset write‑off permanent and reintroducing loss carry‑back that passed the Parliament in August. We’re also providing incentives for start ups and cutting red tape and we’ve expanded eligibility for the 50 per cent active asset Capital Gains Tax concession to all 2.7 million active small businesses. This is an important part of our ambitious tax reform package, which is making the tax system fairer and more sustainable, making it easier to buy a first home and cutting income taxes for workers again and again. The Hon Dr Jim Chalmers MP Treasurer

title: Ambassador to the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Ambassador to the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste Media release 21 September 2026 Today I announce the appointment of Ms Lucienne Manton as Australia’s next Ambassador to Timor-Leste. Timor-Leste and Australia share a long history based on the close friendship between our peoples. In January 2026, Prime Ministers Albanese and Gusmão signed the Parseria Joint Declaration, which sets out priorities for our future development, security and economic cooperation. Australia and Timor-Leste continue to work closely together to advance our shared interests, including Timor’s integration into ASEAN, and the development of the Greater Sunrise gas fields consistent with the 2018 Maritime Boundary Treaty. Ms Manton is a senior career officer with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade and was most recently Assistant Secretary, Mainland South and Central Asia Branch. She has served as Ambassador to Counter Modern Slavery, People Smuggling and Human Trafficking, overseas in the United Kingdom and on a short-term mission as Special Representative on Afghanistan. I thank outgoing Ambassador Caitlin Wilson for her contributions to advancing Australia’s interests in Timor-Leste since 2024. title: Government delivers half a million free mental health appointments
text: Media event date: 20 August 2026 Date published: 20 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public More Australians than ever are accessing free mental health support, with Medicare Mental Health Centres delivering more than 500,000 walk-in appointments nationwide as the Government continues to strengthen Medicare. In 2025-26, almost 24,000 people accessed support through Medicare Mental Health Centres on more than 230,000 occasions. Without Medicare Mental Health Centres, many of these Australians would have faced out-of-pocket costs for care or may not have sought support at all. In total, nearly 50,000 Australians have now turned to Medicare Mental Health Centres for free mental health support, with most presenting for anxiety and mild depression. Medicare Mental Health Centres provide immediate support without the need for a referral or pre-booked appointment, making it easier for Australians to get help when they need it, where they are. To make sure no Australian misses out, the Government is continuing to expand the Medicare Mental Health Centre network, with an additional $267.3 million invested to rollout 32 new or upgraded centres taking the network to 92 across Australia by mid-2030. Staffed by highly trained teams of psychologists, counsellors, social workers, mental health nurses and peer workers, the centres provide a welcoming place where Australians can access free support close to home. For further information on Medicare Mental Health Centres, visit the Medicare Mental Health website or call 1800 595 212. Quotes attributed to Minister Butler: “The Albanese Government is making it easier for Australians to receive the support and care they need when they need it. “No appointment needed, our Medicare Mental Health Centres are providing free face-to-face care to hundreds of thousands of Australians. title: Keeping industry competitive while cutting emissions
text: Keeping industry competitive while cutting emissions Keeping industry competitive while cutting emissions 7 August 2026 The Albanese Government is reviewing the Safeguard Mechanism to ensure it continues to deliver the emissions reductions Australia needs while supporting a strong and competitive industrial base. In 2023, when the Government reformed the Abbott Government’s Safeguard Mechanism, we committed to undertaking a review in 2026-27 to assess whether the mechanism was achieving its emissions reduction objectives and remained fit for purpose beyond 2030. The first two years of operation show the mechanism is working as intended. Gross and net emissions from covered facilities are tracking well, and the scheme remains on course to deliver its proportionate contribution to Australia's legislated 2030 emissions reduction target. With Australia now setting its sights on 2035, this review is focused on ensuring the Safeguard Mechanism continues to drive real, durable emissions reductions across Australia's largest industrial facilities and contributes its fair share to achieving the nation's emissions targets. The consultation paper released today seeks feedback on the policy settings needed to support the Safeguard Mechanism's contribution to the 2035 target, including how to maintain a strong focus on domestic emissions reduction as Australia transitions to net zero. Policy certainty is critical to the investment decisions required to decarbonise industry and transform Australia's economy. The review will consider post-2030 settings while providing a clear and stable framework for emissions reduction over the long term. Importantly, the review is not intended to fundamentally redesign the Safeguard Mechanism. Rather, it will examine how the existing framework can continue to deliver effective emissions outcomes beyond 2030, consistent with its contribution to the 2030 target. The review will place particular emphasis on domestic abatement, industrial decarbonisation and strengthening Australia's energy security through greater electrification and the use of Australian renewable energy. The Safeguard Mechanism Review is scheduled to be completed in early 2027. Feedback on the consultation paper is invited until Friday, 18 September 2026. The consultation paper can be found here https://consult.dcceew.gov.au/2026-27-safeguard-mechanism-review

title: Another record number of companies created in July
text: Another record number of companies created in July 4 August 2026 Another record number of companies created in July New ASIC numbers show that a new record has been set for the number of new companies registered last month. 44,040 new companies were registered in July, this came after 43,393 were registered in June. There have been only two times since records began in 1999 that more than 40,000 businesses have been registered in a month and both times have occurred under the Albanese Labor Government, with the biggest two months for business creation being the two months since the budget. There have now been more than 1.3 million new companies registered under this Labor Government and more than 1.3 million jobs created under this Labor Government. An average of 900 companies have been created each day of this Labor government while just over 30 have become insolvent. There’ve been around 30 times the number of companies opening than closing each day on average on Labor’s watch. Angus Taylor and the Coalition try to talk down our small business sector and talk down our economy. They fail to mention that the insolvency rate is almost half of what we saw in the Howard years and new registrations are at record highs. The Budget contained important new support for small businesses which recognises the legitimate pressures they face. Despite these pressures, we are encouraged by the record numbers of new businesses being created on our watch and the strong growth in business investment. The Hon Dr Jim Chalmers MP Treasurer

title: Strengthening Medicare: Bulk billing on the up
text: Media event date: 10 August 2026 Date published: 10 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Australian Government’s record investment in strengthening Medicare is delivering big benefits for Australians, with access to bulk billing continuing to increase way ahead of schedule. Nationally, the bulk billing rate for the June 2026 quarter rose to 84.1 per cent, up almost five percentage points on the same quarter, last year. Before the Albanese Government started investing in bulk billing, the national rate had fallen to 75.6 per cent. Bulk billing has increased in every state and territory: NSW 87.5% up 4.1 percentage points VIC 85.7%, up 5.7 percentage points QLD 82%, up 4.7 percentage points SA 82.5%, up 6 percentage points WA 76.8%, up 4.8 percentage points TAS 80.8%, up 5.5 percentage points NT 90.8%, up 13 percentage points and ACT 59.3%, up 2.4 percentage points. The bulk billing rate also for patients aged 16 to 64 years had the highest growth – up 8.2 percentage points to 78.6%. There are more than 3,800 Medicare Bulk Billing Practices, over 1,400 of those were mixed billing practices before our Government’s historic investments. A range of Medicare statistics are published quarterly on the Department’s website. Get more information on bulk billing including an additional bulk billing dashboard. Quotes attributable to Minister Butler: “Our government is delivering more bulk billing to more Australians “Across the country more and more GP practices are becoming fully bulk billing clinics meaning all patients need is their Medicare card, not their credit card. “It’s good for patients hip pockets and good for their health.” Minister: The Hon Mark Butler MP Tags: Medicare Strengthening Medicare measures

title: Migrant women to discuss health in their language
text: Media event date: 23 September 2026 Date published: 23 September 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Australian Government is continuing its national program to provide health information and support to migrant and refugee women in their own languages. Through a $10.8 million investment over 2 years, the Multicultural Centre for Women's Health will continue leading the Health in My Language Program in partnership with 7 organisations across the country. Migrant and refugee women can face significant barriers to accessing health information and services, including language differences, lower health literacy and challenges navigating an unfamiliar healthcare system. The Health in My Language Program helps address these barriers by training and supporting bilingual health educators to deliver free, culturally safe health education sessions in participants’ preferred language. Using shared language, evidence-based and up-to-date knowledge, lived experience and strong community connections, educators support women to navigate services and make informed decisions about their health and wellbeing. The sessions provide a safe and supportive environment where women can ask questions, share experiences and build confidence in managing their own health and the health of their families. Since commencing in 2022, the Government has invested around $35 million in the program. More than 8,000 people from migrant and refugee communities across every state and territory have participated in sessions delivered in more than 30 different languages. The investment will continue to address a critical gap in culturally responsive health information and help ensure more women have the information, support and confidence to access services they need. Quotes attributable to the Minister for Multicultural Affairs, Dr Anne Aly: "Language should never be a barrier to accessing important health information, support and services. “This program ensures migrant and refugee women can receive trusted, culturally appropriate information in a language they understand. "By empowering women with knowledge and confidence, the Health in My Language Program is strengthening the health and wellbeing of individuals, families and communities across Australia." Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister White: "Good health starts with having information that is accessible, relevant and delivered in a way that resonates with people’s experience. "What makes this program so effective is that it is delivered by trusted bilingual health educators who understand the communities they work with and create safe spaces for women to ask questions, share experiences and learn from one another. "The evaluation shows these sessions are making a real difference. Women are building confidence, better understanding their health needs and feeling more empowered to navigate the healthcare system. "When women feel informed and supported, the benefits extend far beyond the individual to families. and communities and future generations." Quotes attributable to case studies of women attending Health in My Language sessions: Case study 1 : “Before I started the HIML sessions, I was anxious and overwhelmed whenever I thought about using the healthcare system. I had never attended any health education programs before and due to language barriers… I had no idea how to ask for help or navigate the health system… It left me feeling unsure, isolated, and disconnected from taking care of my health. Today, I feel much more comfortable and confident when using health services. The knowledge I gained gave me the courage to overcome my past hesitations and encouraged me to go to the clinic” Case study 2: “About a year ago, I attended a Health in My Language session about women’s health and cancer awareness. During that session, information about stomach and bowel cancer especially stayed with me. At the time, I remember feeling worried because some of the symptoms discussed sounded familiar to me…After the session ended, I approached the health educator privately and shared my concerns. For the first time, I openly spoke about the symptoms that had been worrying me for a long time. The educator listened carefully, without judgment, and helped me book an appointment with a GP. At the medical appointment, I explained my symptoms and concerns. Even though routine screening was not yet recommended for my age, the doctor decided to organise further medical investigations because of the symptoms I described. After completing the tests, doctors identified changes that required medical attention and early treatment. I was told that addressing the issue early helped prevent more serious complications and possible long-term consequences.” Minister: The Hon Rebecca White MP Tags: Women's health

title: Future Fund’s strong returns continue under modernised investment mandate
text: Future Fund’s strong returns continue under modernised investment mandate 26 August 2026 Future Fund’s strong returns continue under modernised investment mandate Note Joint media release with Senator the Hon Katy Gallagher Minister for Women Minister for Finance Minister for the Public Service Minister for Government Services The Albanese Government welcomes another outstanding return achieved by the Future Fund. These results against a backdrop of ongoing global uncertainty show the Fund’s performance is going from strength to strength and backing the nation’s priorities. The Fund made an annual return of 14.8 per cent for the financial year ending 30 June 2026. This is up from 12.2 per cent for the equivalent period in 2025, 9.1 per cent in 2024 and 6.0 per cent in 2023. This means Australia’s sovereign wealth fund has grown by $37.4 billion in the past year. The Fund’s 10‑year return of 9.0 per cent is above the mandated target return of 7.1 per cent. The Fund continues to deliver strong results as it invests in the nation’s priorities. Since the Fund’s Investment Mandate was updated it has committed $3.5 billion to new direct investments in national priority areas. The Fund invests in national priority areas where it makes financial sense to do so and since the mandate was updated its returns have gone up, not down. The Fund’s average annual returns have been 14.8 per cent and 12.2 per cent in the two financial years after the mandate was updated, compared to 9.1 per cent in the financial year just before it was updated. These results show our opponents were wrong to engage in scaremongering over modernising the investment mandate. The Government thanks outgoing CEO of the Future Fund, Dr Raphael Arndt, for his contribution over many years, including through a period of significant global uncertainty. The Hon Dr Jim Chalmers MP Treasurer

title: Early childhood STEM excellence celebrated in 2026 Little Scientist Awards
text: Release type: Media Release Date: 17 August 2026 Early childhood STEM excellence celebrated in 2026 Little Scientist Awards Ministers: Senator the Hon Dr Jess Walsh Minister for Early Childhood Education Minister for Youth Spotted Frog Kindergarten in NSW is this year’s national winner of the 2026 Little Scientists Early STEM Education Awards. The awards celebrate excellence in inquiry-based STEM education for children aged 0–8 years. The award-winning projects show the many ways inquiry-based learning and child-led STEM activities can be used in early childhood education. These projects encourage children to ask questions, be curious about the world around them, and explore interesting and challenging ideas through hands-on learning. Spotted Frog Kindergarten was recognised for its 12-week project, "Can colours mix without actually mixing?”, which sparked children’s interest as they investigated optical blending, reflection and perception through experiments. The 2026 national and state and territory winners will receive valuable STEM resources and prizes to help educators continue to find fun and practical ways to teach STEM. The Australian Government is supporting the Little Scientists program with $700,000 in funding in 2026-27, helping to empower early childhood educators and teachers to build their skills and confidence to deliver engaging STEM experiences for young children. title: Permanent Bondi Medicare Mental Health Centre to deliver ongoing support
text: Media event date: 26 August 2026 Date published: 26 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Albanese Labor Government is making sure ongoing access to free mental health support is available for the Bondi community, with the permanent Bondi Medicare Mental Health Centre now officially open. In the immediate aftermath of the Bondi tragedy, the Albanese Government moved to provide dedicated mental health support for the community, including the Jewish community and all those affected by the terrorist attack. As part of a $42.9 million mental health support package, the Government established a temporary Medicare Mental Health Centre with a focus on trauma-informed care, while work began on a permanent service for the community. Today, Assistant Minister for Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Emma McBride joined the Member for Kingsford Smith, Matt Thistlethwaite, to officially open the new centre. Located at 241 Oxford Street, Bondi Junction, the Bondi Medicare Mental Health Centre will provide free, walk-in mental health care and support for people experiencing distress, mental health concerns or emotional difficulties – no referral or appointment required. The centre will continue to deliver trauma-focused, support while serving as an open door for anyone in the community seeking help. For people who were visiting Bondi at the time of the attack and want to access support close to home, support is also available through the Government's growing network of Medicare Mental Health Centres across Australia. There are currently 57 centres open nationwide, with the network expanding to 92 locations. The Bondi Medicare Mental Health Centre has been commissioned by Central and Eastern Sydney Primary Health Network and is operated by New Horizons. People seeking support can walk in, call 1800 595 212, or visit www.medicarementalhealth.gov.au . Quotes attributable to Minister Butler: “In the wake of the horrific Bondi terror attack, our Government swiftly put in place a range of services to provide immediate mental health and trauma support for the community. “The Bondi Medicare Mental Health Centre is one of those services, and a now permanent fixture to ensure mental health supports are accessible to those who need them, for years to come.” Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister McBride: “Following the senseless terrorist attack at Bondi last year, the Australian Government acted quickly to provide free and immediate mental health support for those affected. “The Bondi Medicare Mental Health Centre has played an important role in helping members of the community impacted by the attack, and this permanent centre will make sure that high-quality mental health care and support remains available for years to come. “Whether you're experiencing mental health challenges, emotional distress, or supporting a loved one, this centre provides a safe, welcoming and accessible place to seek help. “I want to thank the dedicated staff who have supported the Bondi community with compassion and care through an incredibly difficult period, and who will continue to provide that vital support from this new permanent location.” Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister Thistlethwaite: “This permanent Medicare Mental Health Centre will make sure people in our community have ongoing access to free, high‑quality mental health support close to home. “Whether someone is dealing with trauma, struggling with their wellbeing, or simply needs to talk to a professional, they’ll be able to walk in and get help without delay. “I want to thank the staff who have supported our community through an incredibly difficult time, and who will continue to provide that care from this new centre. This service will be an important part of Bondi’s recovery and a vital resource for our local area.” Minister: The Hon Mark Butler MP The Hon Emma McBride MP Tags: Mental health and suicide prevention

title: Reforms to the legislation governing the Australian National University
text: Release type: Media Release Date: 18 August 2026 Reforms to the legislation governing the Australian National University Ministers: The Hon Jason Clare MP Minister for Education The Albanese Labor Government has commenced consultations on legislative reforms to the Australian National University Act 1991, to be introduced into the Parliament later this year. The ANU is a unique national institution and world-class university. It is also central to the Canberra community and economy. The proposed reforms will modernise the ANU Act, strengthening accountability, representation, appointment processes and institutional culture. Proposed amendments would: • reflect in the ANU Act the best practice governance approach as recommended by the Expert Council on University Governance; • reinforce the ANU Council’s responsibility for institutional culture; • ensure the Council has equal numbers of elected and ministerially appointed members; • require the Council to be representative of the community and include the skills and experience needed for the ANU to fulfil its mission, including higher education governance or public sector experience, financial expertise, gender diversity and First Nations representation; • ensure responsibility for appointing members to the Nominations Committee rests with the ANU Council; • establish ex officio Council membership for the Chair of the ANU Academic Board; and • remove the requirement for the Council to approve Deputy Vice-Chancellor appointments, bringing the ANU into line with other Australian universities. These proposed amendments respond to the advice of the Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency (TEQSA). A consultation paper and the details of the consultation process are available on the Department of Education website . Share on: facebook twitter email print

title: Stronger safeguards for Foreign Arrangements
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Stronger safeguards for Foreign Arrangements Joint media release with: The Hon Matt Thistlethwaite MP, Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade 20 August 2026 The Albanese Government has strengthened and streamlined Australia’s Foreign Arrangements Scheme, with legislation passing the Parliament today to help ensure arrangements are consistent with Australia’s national interest. The reforms modernise the Scheme, which provides Commonwealth oversight of arrangements entered into by states, territories, local governments and public universities with foreign entities. The changes more clearly embed the national interest in legislation, improve risk management, and streamline notification requirements. They also capture evolving forms of international engagement, such as arrangements involving overseas campuses of Australian universities. The reforms implement the recommendations from the 2025 independent review of the Scheme led by Rosemary Huxtable AO PSM. The Government recognises concerns regarding researcher-to-researcher collaboration and will require universities to have appropriate policies and processes in place to identify, monitor and manage associated risks. For the first time, universities will be legally required to assess whether research projects could adversely affect the national interest or be inconsistent with Australia’s foreign policy. The Albanese Government has been consistently clear that universities must play their role in managing risks and this reform will help ensure they do so. Australia is strongly committed to international education and research cooperation that is consistent with our foreign policy. These reforms will help keep Australia open to the world while appropriately managing risk and protecting our national interest. title: Reserve Bank interest rates decision
text: Reserve Bank interest rates decision 29 September 2026 Reserve Bank interest rates decision Today the independent Reserve Bank increased the cash rate by 25 basis points. The war in the Middle East is pushing up inflation and interest rates all around the world but that doesn’t make it any easier for Australians. Australian workers didn’t choose this war, but they are paying a hefty price for it. The war has been a disaster for the global economy. The market is pricing in multiple rate rises in every major advanced economy. While today’s decision was widely expected and anticipated, that doesn’t make it any easier. As the RBA’s statement made clear, the conflict in the Middle East is broadening and pushing up energy prices and inflation around the world. The statement also highlighted the impact of AI‑related demand on global prices for technology‑related goods. Inflation is much lower than its peak, but it is higher than we would like and the conflict in the Middle East is making inflation linger for longer. We recognise people are under pressure and we’re doing something about it by helping with the cost of living, whether it’s through cheaper medicines, more bulk billed doctor visits, higher wages, or more tax cuts. We’re helping with the cost of living at the same time as we manage the budget responsibly and address Australia’s long‑standing productivity challenge. New figures out this week showed the budget position in 2025–26 was $6 billion better than expected in May and the deficit was almost half of what we inherited. Responsible economic management is a defining feature of this Government and particularly important at a time of heightened global uncertainty when higher global yields mean even more pressure on the budget. We know it will take time to shift the dial on productivity, which is why the Budget had the broadest productivity package in decades. When we came to office, inflation was north of six per cent and rapidly rising, it’s now much lower than that. Underlying inflation was almost five per cent, it’s now also much lower. We’re not immune from global pressures but we are better placed and better prepared to confront them, with the equal fastest annual growth compared to all major advanced economies, low unemployment, solid wages growth and much stronger public finances. We’re focused on taking pressure off Australians and addressing inflation while we build a more productive and resilient economy and manage global uncertainty, and today’s decision shows why this is so important. The Hon Dr Jim Chalmers MP Treasurer

title: More EV chargers set for our suburbs
text: More EV chargers set for our suburbs More EV chargers set for our suburbs 8 September 2026 The Albanese Labor Government is making it easier for more Australians to choose cheaper-to-run electric vehicles, with a new round of rebates to install chargers at dealerships across suburban Australia. Dealers, repairers and mechanics can now claim up to $3,000 per EV charging plug, and 80 per cent of the cost of EV-specific workshop tools and equipment, up to a total of $50,000 per site. The expanded support is part of the Government’s DRIVEN program to help Australia’s automotive industry keep up with growing demand for electric vehicles. Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen said the government was helping small businesses, dealerships, repairers and mechanics sell, service and repair more EVs across Australia, while supporting more chargers in suburban areas where EV sales have increased the most. “The Albanese Government’s New Vehicle Efficiency Standard is giving Australians access to more models, and now our investment in charging infrastructure is making it easier and cheaper for Australian families to choose an EV. “As electric vehicle sales overtake petrol car sales for the first time in Australia, now’s the time for dealerships, repairers and mechanics to update and upgrade their facilities so more Australian families can power up at a location closer to home,” Minister Bowen said. “Australians are voting with their wallets for a greater choice of cleaner, cheaper-to-run cars, reducing their exposure to international petrol price shocks.” "This is a welcome and practical expansion of the DRIVEN program at a time when dealers across Australia are investing millions in the tools, equipment and workshop upgrades required to service electric vehicles. “These additional funds will help dealers make that transition with confidence and ensure our customers continue to have access to safe, high-quality vehicle servicing and repairs," said James Voortman, CEO of Australian Automotive Dealer Association. The latest round of the DRIVEN program is open for applications until 30 April 2027, with rebates available for: EV charger purchase and installation – up to $3,000 per plug, within a category cap of $21,000 EV-specific workshop equipment and tools – up to 80% of eligible costs, including tools, protective equipment and workshop upgrades. This announcement comes as electric vehicle sales have overtaken petrol cars for the first time in Australia, as more drivers embrace cheaper running costs and greater choice. New vehicle sales figures for August show EV sales increased 171% compared with the same month last year, while battery electric vehicles outsold petrol cars, with 25,824 sales. Battery electric, plug-in hybrid and conventional hybrid vehicles together accounted for more than half of all new vehicle sales.

title: Australia deploys drone specialists as part of expanded Nepal response
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Australia deploys drone specialists as part of expanded Nepal response Joint media release with: The Hon Dr Anne Aly MP, Minister for International Development The Hon Kristy McBain MP, Minister for Regional Development, Local Government and Territories 03 September 2026 Australia will deploy a team of specialist drone operators to contribute to Nepal’s search and rescue effort and boost our humanitarian support package following the catastrophic floods. The team, including members of Fire and Rescue New South Wales and the Queensland Fire Department, will depart in the coming days as part of a 15-person Disaster Assistance Response Team. They will use advanced drone technology to provide rapid mapping and imaging to support Nepali authorities' search operations. In response to Australia’s ongoing offers of assistance, the Government of Nepal has now requested this support. We stand ready to provide further search, rescue and recovery assistance. The latest deployment is in addition to the 19 Australian personnel already dispatched to Nepal to support the crisis response, including consular and humanitarian officers, Australian Federal Police and Defence personnel. 38 Australians remain unaccounted for. Australian officials are working closely with authorities in Nepal and China to support efforts to establish their whereabouts and provide assistance to their families. The conditions facing search and recovery teams remain extremely challenging. Communications are difficult, infrastructure has been destroyed and many areas are still difficult to reach. Australians have responded to the disaster in Nepal with extraordinary generosity, with over $4 million donated to the Emergency Action Alliance that is providing critical support for recovery efforts. In response, the Australian Government will provide a further $3 million to match public donations. This contribution will enable the delivery of vital shelter, water, sanitation and healthcare, as well as providing children with desperately needed temporary learning spaces. It brings the Australian Government’s ongoing humanitarian support package to a total of $11 million. Australians wishing to donate can visit emergencyaction.org.au . Our thoughts remain with all those waiting for news of family and friends, and with the search and rescue teams working in extraordinarily difficult circumstances. The Australian Government continues to do everything we can to confirm the welfare of those who remain unaccounted for and support their families and loved ones.
