title: First phase of Thriving Kids supports start today
text: Media event date: 1 October 2026 Date published: 1 October 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public Families of children with extra developmental needs can now access expanded information and supports, as part of the Albanese Government’s Thriving Kids program. There will be a gradual rollout of Thriving Kids supports both nationally and across states and territories, with all supports to be in place by 1 January 2028. Families can also access other key resources launching today including the new Thriving Kids Autism Helpline (1300 654 789), which will provide autism-specific information, guidance and connections to relevant supports and services. Delivered by leading autism organisation Amaze, the Helpline is supported by a $24.4 million investment from the Albanese Government. It will operate Monday to Friday from 8.00 am to 7.00 pm and will be accessible through the National Relay Service for families who are Deaf or hard of hearing. Key national services launching today include the new Thriving Kids Information and Resource Hub , delivered by the Raising Children Network. Backed by a $9.7 million investment from the Albanese Government, the Hub will provide families with reliable information, practical resources and guidance to help them understand and support their child's development. Importantly, there will be no changes to access or eligibility to the National Disability Insurance Scheme until 1 January 2028. Children with permanent and significant disability or high support needs will continue to access the NDIS. Thriving Kids will provide supports to children aged 8 and under with developmental delay and/or autism with low to moderate support needs. The Commonwealth will continue to work with state and territory governments as services grow over time. Services will include practical support and connections, including through peer support, parenting groups, facilitated playgroups, and family programs. States and territories will also deliver specialised assistance, for those children who need it, such as occupational therapy, physiotherapy, speech therapy, social workers, psychologists, and low-cost assistive technology, aids or equipment. Further information about Thriving Kids can be found at www.health.gov.au/thrivingkids Quotes attributable to NDIS Minister Jenny McAllister: “Every child learns and grows in their own way. Some children need more time to master everyday skills – like communicating, learning, moving, interacting with others, or managing emotions. “For these kids, getting support early can make a world of difference. It can help them build on their strengths, join in at home, at school and in the community, and build skills for everyday life. “In designing Thriving Kids, we listened to experts and families who have navigated the system and know what needed to change. “Today marks the gradual rollout of Thriving Kids services, and the launch of the new digital hub and national autism phone support service will give families an easy place to start – whether they just have questions about their child’s development or are ready to find practical support. “Importantly, the way people access support under the National Disability Insurance Scheme will not change until full Thriving Kids services are rolled out in January 2028.” Minister: Senator the Hon Jenny McAllister Tags: Disability and carers

title: Dwelling commencements, completions up in June quarter
text: Dwelling commencements, completions up in June quarter 7 October 2026 Dwelling commencements, completions up in June quarter Note Joint media release The Hon Clare O’Neil MP Minister for Housing Minister for Homelessness Minister for Cities New ABS data shows dwelling commencements and completions increased substantially in the June quarter, after the Budget. Commencements and completions are both up in these figures but were both falling when we came to office. These are encouraging numbers but we know they can bounce around from quarter to quarter and that there’s more work to do. There were 52,201 dwelling commencements in the June 2026 quarter, up 7.0 per cent in the quarter to be 14.4 per cent in annual terms. When we came to office, they were going backwards 28.9 per cent in annual terms. There were 47,168 dwelling completions in the June quarter, up 5.8 per cent in the quarter to be 15.9 per cent in annual terms. When we came to office, they were going backwards 7.0 per cent in annual terms. We are tackling housing supply from all angles, including funding enabling infrastructure, building 55,000 social and affordable homes and working with states and territories to streamline approvals. The Hon Dr Jim Chalmers MP Treasurer

title: Joint media release: Boost for cutting edge Australian lithium refining technology in Kwinana
text: Joint media release: Boost for cutting edge Australian lithium refining technology in Kwinana Joint media release: Boost for cutting edge Australian lithium refining technology in Kwinana 7 August 2026 Cutting-edge Australian lithium refining technology is getting a multi-million-dollar boost from the Albanese Government, helping build sovereign critical minerals capability and capture more value from our resources here at home. Through the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA), the Albanese Government is providing over $2.9 million to Electralith Pty Ltd to pilot its innovative ‘R-Box’ lithium refining technology. Located in Kwinana in Western Australia, the R-Box pilot uses electricity to turn lithium contained in liquid waste from mining and processing into high-quality lithium needed to make batteries. R-Box is fully electrified, can operate on renewable power, and uses significantly less water and fewer chemicals while producing fewer emissions than conventional lithium refining. The total project cost is $7.3 million and is expected to take approximately 14 months. Design will commence in 2026, with construction, commissioning and operations progressing over 2027. If successful, Electralith plans broader adoption of its technology in Australia and globally. Critical minerals processing is a key priority under the Albanese Government’s Future Made in Australia agenda, helping Australia move up the global value chain and create new economic opportunities from the resources beneath our feet. Quotes attributable to Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen: “The world is electrifying quickly, global demand for lithium is surging and Australia is perfectly placed to help build the batteries underpinning modern society.” “Sovereign onshore lithium refining capability is critical to Australia’s future, and we are proud to support Australian technology that can refine lithium more cleanly, using less water and producing fewer emissions.” Quotes attributable to Minister for Resources and Northern Australia Madeleine King: “Australia has a responsibility to step up and lead on critical minerals and rare earths globally.” “For too long we’ve let others capture the value of our minerals by processing them offshore.” “Projects like this mean we can refine our lithium right here in Western Australia, in an environmentally friendly way that reduces our water use and climate pollution while at the same time building sovereign capability and bolstering our security.”

title: More support to services under Community Child Care Fund
text: Release type: Media Release Date: 21 January 2026 More support to services under Community Child Care Fund Ministers: Senator the Hon Dr Jess Walsh Minister for Early Childhood Education Minister for Youth Early childhood education and care (ECEC) providers can now apply for funding to help services stay open in communities experiencing disadvantage and vulnerability. Up to $106.9 million is available through the Community Child Care Fund (CCCF) to support early childhood education and care services, particularly in regional, rural and remote Australian communities. The Albanese Labor Government has also extended these grants from the previous two years to three years. Since its introduction in 2018, the Australian Government has provided more than $300 million in CCCF funding to around 1,200 services. This round of CCCF will complement the Building Early Education Fund which is investing in expanding or building services in areas of need across Australia. The building fund will include up to $40 million for operational expenditure to support new sites, in addition to the CCCF. Applications are open until 25 February 2026. For more information visit Sustainability and capital support grant - Department of Education, Australian Government . Attributable to the Minister for Early Childhood Education and Minister for Youth, Jess Walsh: “Every child deserves access to quality early learning – no matter their postcode or what their parents do for work. “We know that quality early education sets up children for the best possible start in life. “The Community Child Care Fund plays a critical role in ensuring services can operate in more disadvantaged areas. “This is also why we’re investing $1 billion through our Building Early Education Fund to build more early learning centres where families need them most, including in the outer suburbs and regions.” Share on: facebook twitter email print

title: Government maintains fuel security
text: Government maintains fuel security Government maintains fuel security 30 May 2026 The Albanese Government will maintain maximum flexibility in the domestic fuel market, by extending the temporary relaxation of the baseline Minimum Stockholding Obligation for petrol and diesel for a further three months. This precautionary action will continue to allow suppliers to hold 20 per cent less diesel and petrol in reserve if they commit to delivering more fuel into the domestic market and regional supply until 30 September 2026. These are the stocks of fuel held in Australia, which must be maintained each week by bulk importers and refineries. Australia’s domestic reserves have hit record levels in recent weeks, as fuel continues to arrive as expected and demand returns to normal levels. Fuel secured through Export Finance Australia is adding a further buffer to our fuel security. Since March, the temporary reduction has been critical in addressing supply chain crunches cause by unprecedented demand, especially in regional Australia. This measure provides ongoing flexibility for industry to respond quickly in the event of another significant spike in demand. Our healthy domestic stockholdings have given Government confidence that a three-month extension strikes the right balance of keeping fuel reserves in good supply, while maintaining flexibility in the local market should global fuel market conditions deteriorate. We continue to see expected ships arrive in our ports but the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to disrupt global fuel markets and those impacts are flowing through to Australia, in higher prices and some supply uncertainty. Even once shipping resumes, the return to normal of the global flow of fuels and goods will take months. Building on the original reduction, companies will only be allowed to continue to relax their storage obligations if they provide and implement a new written plan which demonstrates: They will continue to work closely with the Commonwealth, States and Territories to prioritise and facilitate supply to regional, agricultural or maritime consumers who could face shortages of supply; They will continue reasonable supply to regional distributors and wholesale spot markets (noting these were vulnerable to supply chain disruptions when the crisis started); They will respond to any unusual surges in demand to assist in preventing disruptions to supply and provide prompt notice of any such disruptions (new requirements for this extension). The Government has notified states and territories of this extension. The conflict in the Middle East is having a substantial impact on Australian motorists and businesses and we’re taking decisive action to address this issue. Australia remains at level 2 of the national fuel security plan with a current fuel outlook that is secure. Our work to secure more fuel and build resilience in our fuel sector is already making a meaningful difference. We will continue to respond to this global crisis in Australia’s best interest.

title: Visit to California and New York

Australia is firmly committed to working with our international partners to address these global challenges, and Prime Minister Albanese will reiterate our commitment to climate action, peace and security. title: New data shows more Australians choosing to study teaching
text: Release type: Media Release Date: 31 January 2026 New data shows more Australians choosing to study teaching Ministers: The Hon Jason Clare MP Minister for Education New data shows another big jump in the number of people studying to become a school teacher. Applications to study undergraduate teaching in 2026 have jumped 6.5 per cent and domestic undergraduate university offers have jumped 6.3 per cent. The increase in offers will mean another strong year for people starting a teaching degree after last year the number of domestic students starting a teaching degree jumped 9 per cent. The year before that it jumped 10 per cent. This is good news. Teaching is the most important job in the world and we need more of them. When we were elected the number of people studying teaching was going down. Now it’s going up. This is a team effort. The Australian government and state and territory governments working together. That includes pay rises for teachers and reducing teacher workload. It also included Commonwealth Teacher Scholarships worth up to $40,000 and the introduction of paid prac to provide financial support for teaching students. This year the biggest reforms to teacher training in a generation also kick off. This includes changes to the core content of what students are taught to better prepare them to teach children to read and write and count, and give them the skills they need to manage classroom behaviour. Quotes attributable to Minister for Education Jason Clare: “Being a teacher is the most important job in the world, and we don't have enough of them. “We’re now starting to see this turn around. “I want more young people to leap out of high school and want to become a teacher, rather than a lawyer or a banker. “That’s why we are tackling the teacher workforce shortage with teaching scholarships, reforms to teacher training and paid prac for teaching students.” Applications and Offers for Initial Teacher (ITE) process through TACs 15-Jan-25 15-Jan-26 % change 2025 - 2026 Applications 14,371 15,302 6.5% Offers 9,937 10,559 6.3% Source: University Applications and Offers Collection- Preliminary data collected from Tertiary Admissions Centres as at 15 January each year, Department of Education. Notes: Domestic undergraduate Commonwealth Supported Places for Table A universities first semester study only. Application data include highest preference applications only. Where more than one offer is made to the same applicant by a Tertiary Admission Centre, only one offer is included. Final data are expected to be available in the third quarter of 2026. title: Australian Government set to improve access to affordable contraception across Australia
text: Media event date: 11 September 2026 Date published: 11 September 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public Women across Australia will soon have more choice and better access to long-acting reversible contraception, with leading centres set to provide the gold standard in women’s contraceptive care across the country. The Albanese Government has invested $25 million to establish eight LARC Centres of Excellence to make it easier for women to access long-acting contraception including IUDS and contraceptive implants. As part of the program, women can receive free advice from skilled providers about their contraceptive options, as well as the insertion and removal of IUDS and birth control implants. Long-acting reversible contraceptives are among the most effective forms of contraception available, with effectiveness rates of more than 99 per cent. In addition to preventing unintended pregnancy, some can also help manage heavy menstrual bleeding, period pain and conditions such as endometriosis. Outreach services will support women in regional, rural and remote communities by bringing contraceptive services and training opportunities closer to where people live and work. The centres will be operated by the providers from 31 October: Sexual Health and Family Planning ACT Family Planning Welfare Association of NT Family Planning Australia, NSW True Relationships and Reproductive Health, Qld Family Planning Tasmania SHINE SA Sexual Health Quarters, WA Sexual Health Victoria. The LARC Centres of Excellence are part of the Albanese Government’s landmark nearly $800 million Women's Health Package that is continuing to deliver on its promise of more choice, lower costs and better care for women. Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister White: "We want every Australian woman to know their health is a priority of the Albanese Government and we want women to be able to choose the contraception that works best for them, not simply the option that is easiest to access or the one they can afford. “Long-acting contraceptives are safe, highly effective and can be life changing for some women, but we know they haven’t always been easy to access. “With all eight centres now a step closer to opening their doors, more women will be able to access the information, support and care they need to make the choice that is right for them. “A really important part of these centres is training more doctors, nurses and health professionals, so women can have these conversations and access the care they need closer to home." Minister: The Hon Rebecca White MP Tags: Women's health

title: Australian Government delivers more mental health services for young Western Australians
text: Media event date: 6 September 2026 Date published: 6 September 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Australian Government is expanding access to free mental health care in Western Australia, with a major upgrade to services in Perth's east and a brand-new centre for Perth's growing northern suburbs. Young people and families in Midland and the City of Wanneroo will soon have greater access to free mental health support closer to home, with Headspace Midland set to be upgraded and a new headspace centre to be delivered in Wanneroo. The existing headspace Midland centre, which has already delivered approximately 9,000 free appointments to local young people, will be upgraded to a headspace Plus centre, delivering enhanced support for those with more severe and complex mental health needs. As one of the first 10 headspace services in the country to transition to the new model of care, the Australian Government will deliver a new larger centre for headspace in Midland, expand the workforce of mental health professionals and increase the centre's capacity to support young people and families. A new headspace centre will also be established in the City of Wanneroo, bringing free mental health support to one of Perth's fastest-growing communities. The service will support young people aged 12 to 25 experiencing anxiety, depression, psychological distress and other mental health challenges, making it easier to access care when it's needed most. Both headspace Plus Midland and headspace Wanneroo are expected to open in the next financial year. headspace is Australia's leading youth mental health service and now the world's largest youth mental health network, with 176 centres operating nationwide. The Australian Government has committed more than $211.5 million to deliver 56 new, upgraded or expanded headspace services across Australia, including upgrading 30 centres to the headspace Plus model and expanding the network to more than 200 locations. For young people who prefer digital support eheadspace provides free online and telephone support, making sure help is available wherever they live. For more information, visit www.headspace.org.au or call 1800 650 890. Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister, Emma McBride: “Around two in five young Australians experience mental health challenges every year, which is why early access to support is so important. “The upgrade of headspace Midland and the establishment of a new headspace centre in Wanneroo will help more young people access free mental health care in their local community. “The Albanese Labor Government is expanding access to free mental health services across Western Australia, ensuring more young people can get support early, before their mental health challenges become more serious.” Quotes attributable to Member for Hasluck, Tania Lawrence MP: “I think most of us know a young person who, at some point, has struggled and needed someone to talk to. "Headspace in Midland has provided a trusted and much loved listening ear and support for young people across Hasluck and beyond. "Now, to be delivering this investment to expand Headspace into Headspace Plus will mean services are even easier to access when young people's needs become more complex". "It’s about making sure a young person who is doing it tough can walk through the door and know: someone is here to help me. "Sitting alongside the Midland Kids Mental Health Hub and Midland Medicare Mental Health Centre for adults, the Albanese Labor Government's practical investment in mental health care is delivering services for all ages and needs in Hasluck". Quotes attributable to Member for Pearce, Tracey Roberts MP: "The City of Wanneroo is one of Perth's largest and fastest-growing communities, and it's important our young people have mental health support close to home." "For years, families in Pearce have had to travel to headspace Joondalup, one of the busiest centres in WA, just to access this kind of support." "This new centre means young people and families in Pearce will finally have somewhere local to turn to, while also taking pressure off headspace Joondalup." "This is Community First, backing our growing region with the services it needs, now and into the future." Minister: The Hon Emma McBride MP Tags: Young people's health Mental health and suicide prevention

title: Joint media release: $8.2 million to help Canberrans electrify their homes
text: Joint media release: $8.2 million to help Canberrans electrify their homes Joint media release: $8.2 million to help Canberrans electrify their homes 17 September 2026 The Hon Chris Bowen MP, Minister for Climate Change and Energy Senator the Hon Katy Gallagher, Senator for the ACT The Hon Josh Wilson MP, Assistant Minister for Climate Change and Energy David Smith MP, Member for Bean A new digital tool will help Canberrans make their homes cheaper to run, healthier and more comfortable by offering a one-stop shop for home electrification upgrades. The ‘Go Electric’ tool will simplify the switch from gas to electricity by handling the key parts of the process – from expert advice and fixed-price quotes to installation and ongoing support – making it easier for Canberrans to get the most out of their next home upgrade. Residents of Canberra’s southern suburbs will be the first to try the digital platform in a trial involving up to 1,000 households led by home electrification company Electric Future and supported by $8.2 million from the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA). As well as supporting upgrades to home heating, cooling and appliances, the trial will also help Canberrans make the most of electric vehicles, rooftop solar and home batteries. A key outcome of the project will be to demonstrate how home electrification can be delivered at scale, providing practical insights that can support more households to make the switch over time. The ACT-based trial builds on ARENA’s broader work supporting household and community energy innovation, with around 50 related initiatives funded since 2018 and more than $150 million invested in projects spanning home electrification, smart appliances, flexible energy use and technologies such as virtual power plants. These projects are helping households and communities take greater control of how they generate, store and use energy, cutting bills for homeowners, renters and public housing residents. Quotes attributable to Minister for Climate Change and Energy, Chris Bowen: “Home upgrades can make a big difference to everyday life – not just to comfort and ease of use, but also to your hip pocket and the health of everyone under your roof. “But upgrading your home can feel daunting – you need to work out the right upgrades for your home and your needs, then find someone you trust to install them for the right price. “A one-stop shop providing expert advice, fixed-price quotes, trusted installers and ongoing support will help people make the best choices for themselves, their homes and their families – and gives them the confidence to get on with the job.” Quotes attributable to Senator for the ACT, Katy Gallagher: “Canberrans have been at the forefront of the transition to cleaner energy, and this investment builds on that progress. “Helping households use energy more efficiently and move away from gas is good for household budgets and good for our transition to a cleaner energy system. “This trial will also give us valuable evidence about how we can make electrification easier and more affordable for households at a much larger scale.” Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister for Climate Change and Energy, Josh Wilson: “The built environment is responsible for around a quarter of Australia’s emissions, so improving the energy performance of our homes is one of the most practical ways households can cut costs while contributing to climate action. “This project will help Canberrans make smarter choices about electrification and energy efficiency, creating healthier, more comfortable homes that are cheaper to run and better for the environment.” Quotes attributable to Member for Bean, David Smith: “South Canberra households will be the first to try this new one-stop shop, making it simpler to choose and install the right electric upgrades for their homes. “Canberrans are leading the country in switching to cleaner, cheaper-to-run homes, and this trial will help up to 1,000 local households take the next step. “Whether it’s better heating and cooling, electric appliances, rooftop solar or a home battery, this project will give local families trusted advice and support from start to finish.”

title: $3 million boost to support men's health
text: Media event date: 2 September 2026 Date published: 2 September 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public The Australian Government is investing $3 million to support the mental health and wellbeing of boys and men, by backing new research from Flinders University that responds to significant gaps in evidence and support for boys’ and men’s mental health. This investment will be used to help establish the ‘WellMen’: Centre for the Mental Health and Wellbeing of Boys and Men, which will be led by Professor James Smith of Flinders University. Professor Smith and his team are aiming to improve the mental health and wellbeing of boys and men in Australia by working with them to develop new strategies to promote mental health at critical life stages and in places where they feel most comfortable including schools, sports clubs, and online. The project will also lead to developing, supporting and growing the boys' and men's mental health promotion in the workforce. WellMen will be supported by a range of industry partners including the Movember Institute of Men’s Health, The Man Cave and Deadly Male. This funding forms part of a larger investment of $66 million under NHMRC’s Centre of Research Excellence (CRE) 2026 grant opportunity. The CRE scheme provides support for teams of researchers to pursue collaborative research and develop capacity in basic science research, clinical research, health services research and public health research. Read more about the projects funded on NHMRC’s website . Quotes attributable to Special Envoy for Men’s Health, Dan Repacholi MP: “The Australian Government is proud to support this important research that brings together leading researchers across various facets of men’s health into one integrated, multidisciplinary project. “Too many Australian men and boys are struggling with their mental health, and we need to do more to make sure support reaches them in the places and ways that work for them. “The WellMen CRE is a critical piece of the puzzle that will help us tackle the ongoing national crisis of men’s and boys’ mental health.” Quotes attributable to NHMRC CEO Professor Steve Wesselingh: “Health and medical research have the power to change lives by building the evidence we need to improve health outcomes for people across Australia. “Through NHMRC’s Centre of Research Excellence scheme, we are supporting high quality, collaborative research that can be translated into better policy, practice and care. “This investment will help build the skills, partnerships and research workforce needed to respond to priority health challenges, such as men’s and boys’ mental health and deliver lasting benefits for the community.” Quotes attributable to CRE Director, Professor James Smith: “WellMen intentionally brings together researchers, health professionals, policymakers, industry partners and consumers to co-design mental health research priorities that are critical for advancing boys and men’s mental health and wellbeing in Australia. “WellMen represents a critical milestone in men’s mental health research in Australia, with significant potential to shape mental health promotion and prevention investments that are appropriately tailored to the needs of boys and men, particularly those from marginalised backgrounds. “WellMen provides critical infrastructure to invest in the next generation of men’s mental health researchers in Australia, including stronger national and international research partnerships and co-ordination.” Quotes attributable to Movember Institute of Men’s Health Chief Impact Officer, Professor Simon Rice: “The WellMen CRE will create critical opportunities for capacity development and knowledge gain for men’s mental health scholarship and practice both here in Australia and internationally. The Movember Institute of Men’s Health is proud to be a partner in the CRE, including our direct role with two industry-based researchers embedded within the CRE work”. Quotes attributable to The Man Cave CEO, Ben Vasiliou : “Boys and men in Australia deserve a mental health system that is designed for them, not adapted for them as an afterthought. WellMen gives us a genuine chance to build that, and The Man Cave is ready to make that happen.” Quotes attributable to Deadly Male Board Director, Jason Bonson: “Deadly Male is delighted to be partnering with WellMen researchers to build a stronger evidence base and to support knowledge translation activities. “These activities are aimed at improving Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander male social and emotional wellbeing through community led research that informs strengths based and culturally relevant solutions.” Quotes attributable to nineteen year old Peter Susanto from the Northern Territory: “Investing in ‘WellMen’ does not just mean delivering crucial research to support evidence based, localised and sustainable solutions for creating well men - the ripple effect of boys and men living productive, healthy and peaceful lives benefits the entire community.” Minister: The Hon Dan Repacholi MP Tags: Men's health

title: Australia and China strengthen energy and climate cooperation towards net zero
text: Australia and China strengthen energy and climate cooperation towards net zero Australia and China strengthen energy and climate cooperation towards net zero 27 August 2026 Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen today hosted China’s Minister of Ecology and Environment, Huang Runqiu, for the 10th Australia-China Ministerial Dialogue on Climate Change at Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park. Together, Australia and China are unlocking the economic opportunities of the global clean energy transformation – empowering households to take control of their energy bills through electrification and helping nations make their energy grids more secure and reliable. Ministers discussed the economic opportunities of the global shift to net zero and the opportunity to strengthen energy security while transitioning away from fossil fuels. They underscored the importance of accelerating climate action to achieve net zero by or around mid-century, in keeping with the science. Further to the discussion between Prime Minister Albanese and Premier Li in April, and subsequent Ministerial exchanges, the Dialogue emphasised the importance of both countries working to ensure energy security for both nations, including the continued flow of liquid fuels. With Australia leading COP31 negotiations, Ministers agreed to work together in the lead up to and at COP31 to support global emissions reduction goals, furthering the shared aim of building trade and economic opportunities in both countries and around the world. Ministers Bowen and Huang discussed the benefits of increasing electrification, including economic growth, energy security, job creation and improved public health and downward pressure on household budgets by helping homes take charge of their energy bills. Ministers also welcomed efforts to strengthen emissions accounting and adaptation policy initiatives and agreed to continue our exchange in these areas in the national interest of both countries. Engagement with Beijing on climate change is in line with Australia's broader policy on China of cooperating where we can, disagreeing where we must and engaging in our national interest. Quotes attributable to Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen: “By strengthening understanding and cooperation with one of the world’s largest economies, we are able to strengthen global energy security and help insulate households from global price shocks, in our national interest. “In leading global climate negotiations, Australia is driving practical international action and working with our major trade partners to unlock the economic opportunities of electrification, which is putting downward pressure on energy bills. “I look forward to working constructively with all our international partners, including China, to accelerate electrification and the energy transition in the lead-up to COP31.”

title: $10K incentives backing more Tasmanians into a trade
text: Media event date: 26 August 2026 Date published: 26 August 2026 Media type: Media release Audience: General public More than 800 Tasmanians have kickstarted their pathway to a trade, and with it a good, secure career for their future, backed in by the Albanese Labor Government’s $10,000 incentives for new housing construction apprentices. In the first 13 months of the Key Apprenticeship Program, 801 Tasmanians joined the program, signing up as new apprentices in the housing construction sector and growing the skills pipeline to help build more homes for Tasmanians. Supported by 453 employers across the state, the apprentices will receive five $2,000 incentive payments over the life of their apprenticeship to help with costs such as tools and transport, while also supporting apprentices to stick with their apprenticeship through to completion. Chippies are proving to be the most popular occupations in Tasmania, with 347 apprentice commencements in the program, followed by plumbers (122 commencements) and glaziers, plasterers and tilers (77 commencements). More than half of apprentices are aged 19 or under, showing strong interest from young Tasmanians in building a career in the trades. The industry is also seeing a greater diversity of apprentices starting in critical, home-building trades, with 42 female apprentices backed through the program so far. At 5%, this represents a promising start in growing the number of women in the industry, which more broadly sees around 3% of women working on the tools. Employers also benefit through the program, receiving $5,000 in the first year of the apprenticeship. Around 90% of these employers are small and medium-sized businesses. The Albanese Government is continuing to back apprentices and employers through the Key Apprenticeship Program, with the 2026–27 Budget locking in the program until 2029, including targeted incentives from 2027 for small and medium-sized businesses and Group Training Organisations. Visit www.apprenticeships.gov.au to learn more about the program. Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister White, MP for Lyons: "We need more homes in Tasmania and to build them we need more tradies, which is why our Government is focused on growing the pipeline of skilled workers we need. “It is fantastic to see more than 800 Tasmanians taking up an apprenticeship, including so many young people choosing a trade and building the skills for a good, secure career. "These incentives help with the real costs of starting an apprenticeship, like buying tools and getting to and from work, while also supporting the local businesses that employ and train our next generation of tradies. “Through the Key Apprenticeship Program and Free TAFE, we’re backing aspiring tradies throughout their journey into the industry and beyond.” Minister: The Hon Rebecca White MP Tags: About the department

title: Building Australia’s Asia capability
text: Download the official portrait of the Minister Biography Connect X Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Personal website Contact Subscribe RSS feed Portfolio agencies Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Austrade Tourism Australia Export Finance Australia Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research Australian Secret Intelligence Service Archives Archives from former Ministers Building Australia’s Asia capability Joint media release with: The Hon Tim Watts MP, Special Envoy for Indian Ocean Affairs 26 August 2026 The Albanese Government wants more young Australians to learn a language and build the skills, confidence and connections to engage with our region, including with our close partner Indonesia. Today Foreign Minister Penny Wong, Indonesian Foreign Minister Sugiono and Special Envoy Tim Watts MP joined Collingwood Football Club captain and Bahasa Indonesia speaker Darcy Moore to showcase the important role language and sport can play in bringing Australia and Indonesia even closer together. At the Melbourne Cricket Ground, they met with the Krakatoas Australian-Indonesian AFL team and children learning Bahasa Indonesia from Brunswick North West Primary School through the Australia Awards Indonesian Language Learning Ambassador program. For Australia, giving young people the language skills and cultural understanding to engage with our region is an investment in our future security, prosperity and relationships. In May, the Government announced $2.5 million through the Community Language Schools Grants Program – Fluency in Asian Languages – Round 1 grant to support Asian language learning. Under the Jakarta Treaty signed in February this year, the Australia-Indonesia Institute will receive $11.4 million to expand its cultural exchange and grants programs over 4 years, creating more opportunities for Australians and Indonesians to learn from each other and strengthen ties. The Government is also strengthening Australia's Indonesia capability through the New Colombo Plan , with a renewed focus on priority Asian language learning, longer-term immersive experiences and deeper engagement with Indonesia. Quotes attributable to Foreign Minister Penny Wong: "Darcy Moore is a great example of how learning a language can open doors to new experiences, connections and a deeper understanding of our region. "We want more young Australians to have the opportunity to learn Bahasa Indonesia and other regional languages so that we build greater cultural understanding and connections with our neighbours. "For Australia, building these skills strengthens our ability to confidently engage with our region and supports our future security and prosperity." Quotes attributable to Special Envoy for Indian Ocean Affairs, Tim Watts: "Building Australia's Asia capability is critical to our nation's future. "We want language learning to open doors for young Australians, whether that is through the classroom, an exchange program, study or a career working with our region. "For Australia to succeed in the years and decades ahead, we need a deeper understanding and engagement with our region's languages, cultures, histories, societies and economies." title: Joint media release: $2.5 billion investment in the Hunter’s future
text: Joint media release: $2.5 billion investment in the Hunter’s future Joint media release: $2.5 billion investment in the Hunter’s future 13 August 2026 The Hon Anthony Albanese MP, Prime Minister of Australia The Hon Chris Minns MP, Premier of New South Wales Senator The Hon Tim Ayres, Minister for Industry and Innovation and Minister for Science The Hon Chris Bowen MP, Minister for Climate Change and Energy The Hon Penny Sharpe MLC, NSW Minister for Climate Change and Energy The Hon Yasmin Catley MP, NSW Minister for the Hunter Meryl Swanson MP, Member for Paterson The Hon Kate Washington MP, Member for Port Stephens More than 1,000 Hunter jobs are secure, after the Albanese and the Minns Labor Governments have jointly contributed $2.5 billion to secure the future of aluminium smelting in the region. The joint investment will deliver a long-term renewable energy solution for the Tomago Aluminium smelter that supports commercially sustainable operations beyond 2028 and accelerates decarbonisation of more than 10 per cent of NSW’s electricity grid, supporting and securing the future of one of the state’s most important industrial assets. Tomago Aluminium has agreed to invest at least $1.1 billion in the facility as part of the deal. This includes $100 million to drive further decarbonisation activities at the smelter and undertake an innovative demand-response program to support the NSW grid. This demand-response program aims to position the Tomago smelter as the international leader in electricity demand response and flexibility services. As part of the agreement, the NSW Government’s contribution is capped at $1.225 billion over 10 years from 2029, supporting the long-term future of Tomago and thousands of Hunter jobs. As a result, Tomago Aluminium will continue operating beyond the expiry of its current electricity supply contract on 31 December 2028, providing certainty for workers, local businesses and the future of the Hunter region. Tomago Aluminium is Australia's largest single electricity user. Securing a long-term renewable energy pathway for the smelter is critical to preserving nationally significant industrial capability and strengthens Australia's ability to supply the growing global market for low-emissions aluminium. The joint investment will underpin nearly 3 gigawatts of new renewable generation and firming capacity, strengthening the state's electricity system and supporting long-term energy affordability and reliability for New South Wales. Australia is one of only a handful of countries with an end-to-end aluminium supply chain, spanning bauxite mining, alumina refining, aluminium smelting through to advanced manufacturing. As a major value-added export, aluminium supports jobs, investment and industrial capability while playing a critical role in clean energy technologies, advanced manufacturing and national infrastructure. The arrangements also ensure revenue comes back to the federal government when aluminium prices are high. This means all Australians will benefit from maintaining domestic aluminium capability and sovereignty, with the added benefit of a monetary return on investment from our governments' contributions should aluminium prices rise. This joint investment from the Albanese and Minns Labor Governments will secure 1,000 direct jobs at Tomago aluminium and 5,000 indirect jobs across the Hunter region, supporting a stronger and more resilient industrial future for New South Wales and Australia. Quotes Attributed to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese “In December last year I stood in the rain at Tomago and told the workers ‘we have your back’. “Today, alongside the NSW Government, we deliver on that promise. “This site isn’t just important for Newcastle and the Hunter, it’s a critical asset for the country and our manufacturing future. “I’m proud of the work we’ve done with the company, with the Minns Labor Government, with local members and with the workers here on site to secure Tomago’s future beyond 2028.” Quotes Attributed to New South Wales Premier Chris Minns “This is a good day for the Hunter. This agreement secures more than 1,000 jobs at Tomago and thousands more that rely on the smelter, and gives the region certainty about its future. “I want to thank the Prime Minister and the Commonwealth Government. We’ve worked closely together to get to this point and deliver an agreement that to find a way through and secure the future of Tomago. “The Hunter has powered NSW and helped build this country for generations. This agreement is about making sure it remains an industrial and manufacturing powerhouse for generations to come. “This is part of our bigger plan for the Hunter, securing the good jobs and industries that are here today, while investing $12 billion to bring train manufacturing back to the Hunter and create good, secure jobs for decades to come.” Quotes Attributed to Minister for Industry and Innovation and Minister for Science Tim Ayres “Australia’s end to end aluminium industry - from bauxite to complex aluminium finished products - is critical for Australia’s national resilience. Tomago is Australia’s largest and youngest smelter and is crucial to Australia’s industrial future. ”Keeping this capability here in Australia matters. It makes our economy stronger, drives new electricity projects and maintains thousands of good quality blue collar and engineering jobs right here in the Hunter. “The Albanese Government is delivering a Future Made in the Hunter: good regional jobs, more industrial and energy investment and stronger regional economies.” Quotes Attributed to Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen "Tomago Aluminium has made it clear: to remain competitive and secure its future the smelter needs a reliable and affordable supply of renewable energy, with ageing coal-fired power options being prohibitively expensive. "We're fighting for the regions and bringing more renewables online faster – so we can deliver the modern and affordable energy grid Australian's deserve and industry needs." Quotes Attributed to NSW Minister for Climate Change and Energy Penny Sharpe “This investment secures more than 1,000 local jobs and connects key manufacturing to a long-term pathway to run on renewable energy. “It shows we can protect the industries and workers that power the Hunter while building a cleaner energy future in NSW." Quotes Attributed to NSW Minister for the Hunter, Yasmin Catley “Hunter workers and their families deserve certainty, and we have delivered it. “Securing Tomago means securing jobs, skills and the future of our region. “We said these jobs are worth fighting for and today that fight has delivered. “The Hunter builds things and it powers our state. We have the skills, the workers and the industrial muscle, and I am incredibly proud to be part of a government that is willing to back the Hunter and everything we have to offer.” Quotes Attributed to Member for Paterson Meryl Swanson "Hunter workers have helped make Tomago Aluminium one of Australia’s most important manufacturing assets, and today’s announcement provides certainty for the people, families and businesses who depend on it. “As demand for aluminium continues to grow worldwide, with forecasts suggesting we’ll need around 40 percent more of it in the future, it is critical that Australia remains a producer and manufacturer of this essential material. "We’re protecting local jobs, supporting local industry and ensuring the Hunter remains a manufacturing powerhouse for decades to come." Quotes Attributed to Member for Port Stephens Kate Washington "This is a massive investment in local families and our local economy. Tomago Aluminium is one of the largest employers in Port Stephens, and securing its future has been an absolute priority for me and the Minns Labor Government."

title: Cleaner, cheaper energy and cars drive down emissions
text: Cleaner, cheaper energy and cars drive down emissions Cleaner, cheaper energy and cars drive down emissions 29 May 2026 Australia’s emissions have fallen by 9.7 million tonnes over the past year, with more renewable energy, cleaner cars and practical emissions reduction in industry helping drive the decline. The latest Quarterly Update of Australia’s National Greenhouse Gas Inventory shows emissions for the year to December 2025 were 2.1 per cent lower than the previous year, with lower coal, gas and petrol use cutting electricity emissions by 3.8 per cent and transport emissions by 0.6 per cent. This is the second consecutive annual fall in emissions for transport pollution outside of COVID, suggesting Australia’s overall transport emissions may have peaked as more motorists choose cleaner, cheaper to run vehicles. Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen said this was a positive trend. “EVs have grown from less than 4 per cent of new light vehicle sales in 2022 to more than 20 per cent in the first four months of 2026. Our New Vehicle Efficiency Standard is making sure Australians get more choice of efficient vehicles that save money at the bowser and cut emissions.” Meanwhile more renewables and battery storage are changing the grid for the better. In 2025, battery discharge in the National Electricity Market (NEM) almost tripled compared to 2024, reducing expensive gas-powered generation during evening peaks by 30 per cent. Alongside record-breaking wind generation and strong large-scale solar generation, the battery boost pushed gas generation to its lowest quarterly level since 2000, resulting in the cleanest NEM Australia has ever seen with 0.44 tonnes of emissions per megawatt hour, and NEM emissions 32 per cent lower than 2005 levels. Minister Bowen said the results showed the practical benefits of building Australia’s cleaner, cheaper and more reliable energy system. “The latest quarterly update is further proof that what’s better for the planet is better for your pocket; more of the cheapest form of new energy, more storage to back it up, and lower emissions as a result,” Minister Bowen said. “With over 4 million household solar systems and more than 400,000 home batteries supported by our Cheaper Home Batteries Program, we’re seeing the results of consistent and considerable cuts in electricity grid emissions.” The results come as the Coalition has promised to scrap Australia’s emissions reduction targets, pause the cheapest new energy coming into the grid, and rely more on ageing unreliable coal. Falling emissions across transport, electricity and stationary energy were partially offset by increased emissions from industrial processes and product use, mainly due to increased steel production. The Albanese Government’s reformed Safeguard Mechanism is also delivering real reductions from Australia’s largest industrial facilities. Net emissions from Safeguard facilities fell 5.5 per cent over the year and are now more than 12 per cent lower than when reforms began. Facilities are installing new technology to cut potent nitrous oxide emissions, using electrification and deploying carbon capture and storage where it can reduce industrial emissions. Some of these projects have reduced nitrous oxide emissions from their facilities by 95% or more. Australia’s overall emissions in the year to December 2025 are estimated to be 24.5% below 2005 levels, reflecting the incorporation of updated Land Use, Land Use Change and Forestry sector estimates from the National Inventory Report 2024 released earlier this year. Land sector emissions are subject to ongoing variability, reflecting both improvements in measurements and the impact of extreme weather events such as La Niña. The National Inventory Report 2024 data reflected updated measurements for previous years as data becomes more precise but also confirmed the downwards trend in emissions overall. Australia is making steady progress in emissions reduction, backed by practical policies including the Capacity Investment Scheme to boost cleaner, cheaper renewable energy and the reformed Safeguard Mechanism and New Vehicle Efficiency Standard to cut emissions. The quarterly update of Australia’s emissions is available at https://www.dcceew.gov.au/climate-change/publications/national-greenhouse-gas-inventory-quarterly-update-december-2025

title: EV sales overtake petrol cars for the first time
text: EV sales overtake petrol cars for the first time EV sales overtake petrol cars for the first time 4 September 2026 Electric vehicles sales have overtaken petrol cars for the first time in Australia in August, as more drivers embrace cheaper running costs and greater choice. New vehicle sales figures for August show more than 27,000 battery electric vehicles were sold, 24.9% of all new vehicle sales and a new monthly record. Electric vehicle sales increased 171% compared with the same month last year, while battery electric vehicles outsold petrol cars, with 25,824 sales. Battery electric, plug-in hybrid and conventional hybrid vehicles together accounted for more than half of all new vehicle sales. Analysis from the National Automotive Leasing and Salary Packaging Association estimates working Australians who accessed the Electric Car Discount in the first half of this year are expected to save $76 million this year alone. Outer-suburban communities are leading the uptake of the discount, with Tarneit, Werribee, Kellyville, Marsden Park and Baulkham Hills among the top postcodes. Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen said the figures marked an important shift in Australia’s car market. “This is a landmark moment as electric vehicles have overtaken petrol cars for the first time in Australia,” Minister Bowen said. “The Coalition said EVs would end the weekend. Seven years later, they’re Australia’s most popular type of new car. “Australians have seen through the scare campaigns and are voting with their wallets for cars that are cheaper to run, cleaner and reduce their exposure to international petrol prices shocks. “The Albanese Government’s New Vehicle Efficiency Standard is giving Australians access to more models, while our Electric Car Discount and investment in charging infrastructure are making it easier and cheaper to choose an EV.”

title: New inflation figures
text: New inflation figures 29 July 2026 New inflation figures New data from the Australia Bureau of Statistics shows headline inflation moderated in both monthly and quarterly terms and monthly trimmed mean was steady. This means that inflation has come in lower than expected, lower than forecast in the Budget or by the Reserve Bank. This is the third consecutive month where annual headline inflation has moderated. It’s an encouraging outcome that shows we’ve made progress on inflation since the Budget, even in the face of intense global uncertainty. The Treasury, the Reserve Bank and others forecast headline inflation to be in the high fours and even five per cent, but today it has come in at 3.9 per cent, and that’s a better outcome in volatile global circumstances. In the monthly data, headline inflation was 3.8 per cent in the 12 months to June, down from 4.0 per cent in May. In month‑on‑month terms headline inflation fell again, by 0.1 per cent in the month of June. In the quarterly data, headline inflation was 3.9 per cent through the year to the June quarter 2026, down from 4.1 per cent through to the March quarter. In quarterly terms, inflation more than halved in the June quarter. Headline inflation was 0.6 per cent in the June quarter down from 1.4 per cent in the March quarter. We already had an inflation challenge in our economy but the war is making it higher than it would otherwise be. Treasury has warned that the next phase of the conflict could be more challenging for the global economy, with the oil market now more vulnerable. While the oil price has fallen around 12 per cent since the end of last week, it remains around 22 per cent higher compared to when the conflict started. The initial impact from the conflict on inflation came from fuel but we see it broadening today in other areas such as dwelling construction costs. Trimmed mean inflation was steady at 3.6 per cent in the 12 months to June. In the quarterly data, trimmed mean was 3.6 per cent through the year to the June quarter, compared to 3.5 per cent in the March quarter. Inflation has gone up since March in most major advanced economies but has come down here. Inflation remains much lower than we inherited. When we came to office, headline inflation was north of 6 per cent and rapidly rising, it’s now much lower than that. Underlying inflation was around 5 per cent but it is now much lower. We understand people are under pressure which is why we’re rolling out responsible cost of living relief including cutting taxes five times in three ways, cheaper medicines and higher wages. From this month, more than 14 million Australian taxpayers got another tax cut, the National Minimum Wage increased by 6 per cent, paid parental leave was extended, and around 2.6 million Australians benefitted from regular indexation of social security payment rates and thresholds. Australia is not immune from global uncertainty, but we’re well placed and well prepared to confront it with faster growth than almost every major advanced economy, booming business investment, low unemployment, solid wages growth and stronger public finances. We’ve made progress in the economy, but there’s more work to do because people are still under pressure. That’s why addressing inflation and helping with the cost of living was a big focus of the Budget and it’s a big focus of the government alongside building a more productive and resilient economy. The Hon Dr Jim Chalmers MP Treasurer

title: Deputy Chair appointments to the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority
text: Deputy Chair appointments to the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority 3 July 2026 Deputy Chair appointments to the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority The Albanese Government will recommend to the Governor‑General that Therese McCarthy Hockey and the Hon David Bradbury be appointed as Deputy Chairs of the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) for five‑year terms. These appointments bring the best available mix of strong leadership, experience and fresh thinking to the regulator. The appointment of two Deputy Chairs will enhance APRA’s capability to meet its objectives at a time of increasing scale and complexity in the financial system. Ms McCarthy Hockey is currently an APRA member and brings more than 20 years’ experience in financial markets having worked internationally and domestically in senior leadership roles in the private sector, in addition to her role at APRA overseeing banking supervision, strategy, risk and compliance. She has an extensive background in regulation, litigation and enforcement and expertise in prudential oversight, governance and protecting financial system stability. We will recommend Ms McCarthy Hockey commence as Deputy Chair on 9 July 2026. Mr Bradbury brings more than 25 years’ experience across economic policy, regulation and public administration. He is currently Chair of the Board of Taxation, has held senior leadership positions at the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development for more than a decade, and was a partner in the consulting division at KPMG Australia. He is also an Honorary Professor at The Australian National University. Mr Bradbury served as Parliamentary Secretary to the Treasurer and Assistant Treasurer between 2010 and 2013. We will recommend Mr Bradbury commence as Deputy Chair on 1 September 2026. Ms McCarthy Hockey and Mr Bradbury were successful in a merit‑based selection process chaired by Treasury Secretary Jenny Wilkinson, with APRA Chair John Lonsdale and Attorney‑General’s Department Secretary Katherine Jones PSM serving on the selection panel. We thank Margaret Cole for her service as APRA Deputy Chair. She has made a significant contribution to strengthening prudential oversight and supporting the resilience of Australia’s financial system. The Hon Dr Jim Chalmers MP Treasurer

title: Vale Professor Peter Buckskin
text: Release type: Media Release Date: 22 May 2026 Vale Professor Peter Buckskin Ministers: The Hon Jason Clare MP Minister for Education I am deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Professor Peter Buckskin PSM FACE —a proud Narungga man, respected leader, educator and tireless advocate for First Nations education. Professor Buckskin’s distinguished career was defined by an unwavering commitment to improving educational outcomes of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students and educators, and a firm belief in the transformative power of education. His work spanned decades of leadership, policy influence and community engagement, leaving a profound legacy across Australia’s education system. Professor Buckskin brought insight, integrity and deep cultural authority to critical discussions shaping policy and practice. A hallmark achievement of his career was the More Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Teachers Initiative (MATSITI), which he led from 2011 to 2016 and supported collaborative workforce projects, research and a campaign to increase the First Nations teaching workforce. He engaged with governments across a range of Indigenous Affairs matters, with recent education forums including Indigenous Education Consultative Meetings, and as a member of the National Respectful Relationships Education Expert Working Group. As Inaugural Chair of the National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Education Corporation (NATSIEC), Professor Buckskin’s knowledge, leadership and generosity of spirit strengthened collaboration and helped drive a shared vision for equitable, culturally responsive education. This leadership was integral to the establishment of the Partnership Agreement between Education Ministers and NATSIEC, and the inclusion of NATSIEC representatives in Education Ministers Meeting to ensure First Nations learners are at the centre of education decisions. Professor Buckskin’s legacy will live on in the many students, educators and communities he inspired, and in the education systems and reforms he helped shape. On behalf of the Australian Government and the Department of Education, I extend my deepest condolences to Professor Buckskin’s family, community and his many friends and colleagues. title: New Commissioners appointed to the Australian Tertiary Education Commission
text: Release type: Media Release Date: 19 January 2026 New Commissioners appointed to the Australian Tertiary Education Commission Ministers: The Hon Jason Clare MP Minister for Education Professor Tom Calma AO and the Hon Fiona Nash have been appointed commissioners of the interim Australian Tertiary Education Commission (ATEC). Professor Calma is the new acting First Nations Commissioner. Professor Calma brings more than four decades of leadership in human rights, social justice and higher education to the role, including as Chancellor of the University of Canberra (2014–2023) and Professor of Practice (Indigenous Engagement) at the University of Sydney. The Hon Fiona Nash was a member of the Australian Universities Accord Panel and is the Regional Education Commissioner. She is a former Minister for Regional Development, Regional Communications and Local Government and Territories and previously held senior roles in regional engagement and government relations at Charles Sturt University. They will join existing commissioner Professor Barney Glover AO, who has been appointed acting Chief Commissioner. Professor Glover is the current JSA Commissioner and a former Vice-Chancellor at several Australian universities. Recruitment of the statutory ATEC Commissioners has commenced, with applications due on 29 January 2026. Subject to the passage of enabling legislation, statutory Commissioner appointments will be announced in due course. Quotes attributable to Minister for Education Jason Clare: “The Universities Accord is a blueprint for reform of our higher education system for the next decade and beyond. “Professor Glover, Professor Calma and Fiona Nash are outstanding leaders who with their deep knowledge and expertise will continue driving the reforms we need to make the Accord real.” Share on: facebook twitter email print
